items.text: A Good Time

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It reflects your inner thoughts, like a mind's endoscope. I cast an arcane skill on it to help your thoughts surface.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Look at it, and tell me what you see.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Have I?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Did I ever look into it? Look into myself.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Before it shattered?

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: What is this thing?

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: The color and design are vulgar, and I don't see our family crest on it. Such a hand mirror is unsuitable for a lady.

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: Even though the surface of the mirror is rather smooth, it simply cannot do.

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: Klara Vingler, you cannot take this as your first hand mirror.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I neither seek your opinion nor your approval, Father.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm simply here to inform you that I have my first hand mirror. There's no longer any need for you to give me one.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: That's all.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: No, wait—

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Father, it's a gift and a blessing from Klara's friend. I think that's why this hand mirror means so much to her.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: And you, Klara—

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: Her friend? What friend?! This isn't that damnable gypsy again, is it? Or one of those filthy arcane vendors, scurrying around in the shadows like rats?

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: No matter who it was, the moment you brought this thing into our house, it was a humiliation to me and to the whole Vingler family!

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: "Your first hand mirror"? Hah! Don't be ridiculous!

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: It isn't qualified to be a Vingler mirror. In fact, it tarnishes our very name! I warned you not to try to win my approval with an inferior product—

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: Inferior like your "friends"!

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Father! This is too much.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Elbert, I've fulfilled my promise. I showed him, and from now on, this is my mirror.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm leaving.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Klara wait! Just a moment.

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: Wherever she's going, she cannot take that mirror with her. I won't allow it.

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: Take that thing away from her, Elbert!

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Father, please. Let her keep it, will you? You can give her another one as her first official hand mirror.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: She didn't mean to—

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: "She didn't mean to"?! She meant every word! She spends her life on her "career" and "ambition" and pays no mind to the shame it brings to this family!

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: As long as she continues to lead such a shameless life, my humiliation will never come to an end!

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Father—

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Haha.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Arcane vendors like rats? Need I remind you how you made your fortune?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: If the Vingler name is truly as noble as you claim, then why do the gentlefolk of the upper class always decline your invitations?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You've worked so hard, haven't you? To hide away your past as an arcane vendor and wear the mask of a noble man.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Or, should I say, a noble human.

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: You—You—

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You know I'm right. I'm simply telling the truth.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The more you try to distance yourself from your arcanist identity, the more people are reminded of it.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: When you criticize Mother for keeping in touch with her arcanist friends, you don't realize it's because YOU don't have any friends anymore, and somewhere deep inside, that stings.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I pity you, to be honest. At least I have true friendship.

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: KLARA VINGLER!

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: What right do you have to accuse me?! You, who have dropped out of university, had multiple scandals with married women, and started an illegal organization?!

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: But you are right about one thing. It's not your patients who should be sent to the madhouse,

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: it's you!

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Father! Do we have to end it this way?

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: Take it from her, Elbert.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Klara—
The servants block the door like silent statues.
She cannot leave unless she gives him the hand mirror.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: No need.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'll do it myself.
She raises the mirror high above her head and throws it to the ground.
It shatters as it collides with the floor. Mirror shards scatter around the room.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Klara.
Her eyes are firmly fixed on her father.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: This is the last time I do as you ask, Father.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Yes, it shattered.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: How could I see myself in it?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I never even had the chance.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It was destroyed, like the table mirror that shattered in the "Storm."
Kakania gives a weak smile, but soon freezes.
She sees the broken table mirror, sees the rain in Vienna.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The hand mirror was too broken, Doctor.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I couldn't see myself in it, so I decided to let it go.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "It's insignificant," I thought. "There are far more important things to come!" How naive I was to not see ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Our society is broken, and like a mirror, it will keep shattering into ever smaller pieces.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: No one can put them back together on their own.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: So it is my duty, Doctor, to appeal to the people—to urge them to face the problems in our society, to do something to change it, to repair it.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: How ironic that, in the end, I would be the one to hasten the breaking of it beyond repair.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Why me? Why did I survive?

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: I can see why you'd think this way.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: But I think you keep saying this because ...

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: You're still blaming yourself.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What else can I do?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Take this shameful event for granted? Feel lucky and cheer for my "second life"?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Why should a girl so full of sin survive? What about those innocent people who still had hope for life—who wanted to survive in this world? They turned to dust and were washed away by the "Storm."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Why did they die? What was the meaning of it?

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: So you looked away because you couldn't face yourself in the mirror.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: But you won't often find answers unless you look for them.
She hangs her head at this gentle accusation.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: At least give it a try.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Take a look at yourself in your own mirror.
